questions.stemHtml: The image shows membrane potential during action potential. The region marked as D-E is due to ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Efflux of K+

The region marked between D and E in the action potential curve indicates repolarization due to the efflux of K+ ions across the cell membrane.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 67

questions.topic: eGurukul · Physiology - INI CET NOVEMBER 2022 (PART - A)
questions.stem: A woman has vomiting whenever she eats spicy food. Arrange the sequence of events during vomiting?Contraction of diaphragm and abdominal musclesInspiration against closed glottis LES opens and UES opensReverse peristalsis in small intestineChoose the correct answer from below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
BDAC

The correct sequence of events during vomiting is:-

B: Inspiration against closed glottis (the glottis is the opening between the vocal cords in the larynx)

D: Contraction of diaphragm and abdominal muscles

A: LES (Lower Esophageal Sphincter) opens and UES (Upper Esophageal Sphincter) opens

C: Reverse peristalsis in the small intestine

Therefore, the correct answer is C. BDAC.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 837

questions.topic: eGurukul · Physiology - INI CET NOVEMBER 2022 (PART - A)
questions.stemHtml: The below graph shows the Oxygen-dissociation curve. The curve marked as A indicates ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Myoglobin
  • The curve 'A' shows a hyperbolic curve that is characteristic of oxygen dissociation in myoglobin.
  • Myoglobin is an iron-containing component of the skeletal muscle. Myoglobin can bind only to one oxygen molecule and hence lacks cooperative binding.
  • It has a higher affinity to oxygen than hemoglobin and hence releases oxygen only at low PO2 values. This leads to a leftward shift in the myoglobin oxygen dissociation curve.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No. 712, 632.

questions.stem: 2,3 BPG causes unloading of oxygen to tissues because :-

options.label: A
options.text: Decreases ATP production and breaks the link between globin chain

options.label: C
options.text: Binds to central cavity of hemoglobin by histidine and favor salt bridge formation

questions.answerText: Binds to central cavity of hemoglobin by histidine and favor salt bridge formation
questions.solutionHtml:
Binds to central cavity of hemoglobin by histidine and favor salt bridge formation

2,3- Bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG) is an important regulator of the binding of oxygen to hemoglobin. 2,3-BPG is synthesized from an intermediate of the glycolysis.



Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No. 710

questions.stem: Macula densa is made of specialized cells located at?

options.label: A
options.text: Junction of thick descending limb and DCT

options.label: B
options.text: Junction of thick descending limb and PCT

options.label: C
options.text: Junction of thick ascending limb and DCT

options.label: D
options.text: Junction of DCT and collecting duct

questions.answerText: Junction of thick ascending limb and DCT
questions.solutionHtml:
Junction of thick ascending limb and DCT

Macula densa are the specialized cells present at the distal end of the thick ascending loop of Henle, where it reaches the glomerulus. Distal roluted tubule starts from macula densa.



Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No. 342,662.

questions.stem: The primary second messenger involved in the contraction of ciliary muscle during focussing on a near object is?
questions.solutionHtml:
IP3 and DAG
  • Together, IP3 and DAG play a crucial role in the regulation of calcium release and protein kinase activation, respectively, leading to the contraction of the ciliary muscle during focusing on near objects.
    • Contraction of ciliary muscle occurs by the parasympathetic nervous system.
    • M3 receptors which act via DAG and IP3 pathway


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 60,255. Harpers Illustrated Biochemistry, 30th Edition, Page No. 652

questions.topic: eGurukul · Physiology - INI CET NOVEMBER 2022 (PART - A)
questions.stem: How do you calculate cerebral perfusion pressure ?
questions.solutionHtml:
MAP- ICP

Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) is calculated as mean arterial pressure (MAP) - intracranial pressure (ICP).



Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No. 984, 596.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Physiology - INI CET NOVEMBER 2022 (PART - A)
questions.stem: Fluid leaving the PCT in the absence of ADH is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Isotonic

In the absence of ADH, the fluid leaving the PCT is isotonic, maintaining an equal concentration of solutes as in the surrounding interstitial fluid.



Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No. 712.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Physiology - INI CET NOVEMBER 2022 (PART - A)
questions.stem: Normal amount of Insensible water loss per day in the human body?
questions.solutionHtml:
700ml
  • In human beings, there is a loss of water through vaporization from the respiratory tract (300-400 mL) and diffusion from the skin (300-400 mL). This is called insensible water loss.
  • It is about 700 mL/day or 50 ml/hour. This insensible water loss via the skin is independent of sweating and occurs in people without sweat glands as well.
  • To reiterate,  (700ml) is the closest approximation to the normal range of insensible water loss, but it's important to note that individual variation and environmental factors can affect this value.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page No. 305.
